At every maximizing point the canonical masses give V(1−lambda_i)^d+t≥Gamma V, implying the uniform one-sided O(t) bound after a root. The sum-one identity yields the reverse bound, and invertibility of the barycentric chart gives uniform displacement O(t).

On the ball uniform convergence of the affine forms gives a lower sandwich by the fixed open +delta cap and an upper sandwich by the fixed closed −delta cap, allowing the escaping mass. Each residual p_i−kappa ell_i((y_t−g)/t)−pbar is at least −o(1), and their exact zero sum forces each to converge to zero. overlap.comparison: The all-normal ordinary first variation for a fixed added facet strip is the specialization with t equal to the strip volume and a normalized weighted facet law. Its hypotheses and conclusion do not give the general weak-addition theorem, the complete optimizer displacement, or the sharp incidence range.

The projected N=2 thin-cone value follows from one particular limit law after dividing by two. That fact has a fixed simplex family and does not assert the arbitrary-law first variation or every maximizing selection.
